claim: The 4x4 PPT/Schmidt-number-at-least-three target holds iff there exist real-algebraic Hermitian rho,W such that rho is an extreme normalized PPT state, W is an extreme point of the trace-one 2-block-positive slice, and Tr(W rho)<0. Necessarily rho and rho^Gamma have ranks r,s with 2<=r,s<=15, r^2+s^2<=257 and min(r,s)<=11; W has a normalized Schmidt-rank-at-most-two zero; and W has between one and four strictly negative eigenvalues. This is an exact full-target equivalence and reduction, not an assertion that the reduced pair exists.
compact_witness_slice: Let C_2 be the cone of Hermitian 16x16 matrices nonnegative on Schmidt-rank-at-most-two vectors. For nonzero W in C_2, Tr W>0: in any product orthonormal basis all sixteen diagonal expectations are nonnegative and sum to Tr W. If this trace were zero then every product-vector expectation would vanish, because each product vector belongs to such a basis; product projectors span Herm(16), forcing W=0. Consequently B={W in C_2: Tr W=1} is closed. Every normalized product-vector expectation of a member of B lies in [0,1], since the vector extends to a product basis whose nonnegative expectations sum to one. Product projectors span Herm(16), so this uniformly bounds every matrix entry; B is compact and convex.
both_extreme: Given a PPT rho_0 of Schmidt number at least three, separation supplies a nonzero W_0 in C_2 with Tr(W_0 rho_0)<0. Normalize W_0 to trace one, minimize Tr(W rho_0) over compact B, and choose an extreme minimizer W_*. It is extreme in all of B because the minimizers form a face, and it still detects rho_0. Now minimize Tr(W_* rho) over the compact normalized PPT set and choose an extreme minimizer rho_*. The pairing remains negative and rho_* is extreme in the whole PPT set. The converse follows from W_* being 2-block positive. The rank-pair inequality and lower/upper rank bounds follow from the preceding packet's support-intersection argument.
rank_two_zero: If W_* were strictly positive on the compact set of normalized Schmidt-rank-at-most-two vectors, it would lie in the interior of C_2. It could then be written as the average of W_*+epsilon D and W_*-epsilon D for any sufficiently small nonzero traceless Hermitian D, both lying in B, contradicting extremality. Thus some normalized rank<=2 X has <X|W_*|X>=0.
negative_index: W_* has at least one negative eigenvalue because it pairs negatively with a PSD state. Its strictly negative eigenspace V is a complex linear subspace containing no nonzero rank<=2 coefficient matrix. The projective rank<=2 determinantal variety of 4x4 complex matrices has complex dimension 2(4+4-2)-1=11 in projective 15-space. By the projective dimension theorem over the complex numbers, every projective linear subspace of dimension at least 4 intersects it. Therefore dim_C V<=4. The dimension theorem is a named external mathematical import; this is a general 2-block-positive spectral constraint, not a numerical check.
algebraic_pair: For rho and W simultaneously, PPT, trace normalization, negative pairing, and extremality in their respective compact convex sets are expressible by a finite first-order formula over the ordered reals with rational coefficients. Extremality is stated by quantifying over two distinct normalized PPT states or two distinct trace-one 2-block-positive witnesses whose midpoint equals the candidate. Membership in C_2 itself is the universal polynomial test on rank<=2 matrices. The formula has a real solution by the preceding construction, and transfer for real closed fields gives one whose real and imaginary entries are real algebraic. This is a named import, not a computation.
